name: Shelesh
overview: Shelesh was a male member of the tribe of Asher, identified uniquely as the son of Hotham. The biblical record mentions him specifically in 1 Chronicles 7:35. Beyond his tribal affiliation and paternal connection, no additional personal details or notable actions are documented.
namesAndTitles: The name Shelesh is a proper name that means 'triplet' and possibly also 'obedient' or 'gentle' in Hebrew. This name was not given by God but reflects common naming practices of the time as recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:35.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shelesh as the son of Hotham, establishing his direct paternal lineage. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical text beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Shelesh's mention in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles highlights his role in preserving the lineage of the tribe of Asher. While the Bible does not attribute specific deeds or theological significance to him, his inclusion serves to maintain the continuity of God's covenant people through their tribal and familial lines.
